newsitem.title: USA: OCC's Ludwig concerned about syndicated credits.
newsitem.headline: OCC's Ludwig concerned about syndicated credits.

text.p: U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig said in an interview with Massachusetts Banker distributed Friday that he has concerns about the syndicated credit market.

"In today's market, a variety of factors have coalesced in such a way that downstream participants in syndicated deals are frequently left with thinner margins and less than desirable underwriting standards," Ludwig said. He did not cite any specific examples.

Ludwig was responding to a question about what he was hearing from OCC field examiners that bankers should watch out for. He said in some of the syndicated deals, pricing does not appear to adequately reflect risk. He called for the banking industry to exercise heightened discipline.
On the question of the U.S. bank regulatory structure, Ludwig said any change must ensure that supervision of comparable activities should be consistent.
Ludwig said he disagrees with an argument that banks have an unfair advantage against other types of financial service firms due to the deposit insurance system.
Ludwig said studies show that no net subsidy exists because banks are subject to significant regulatory burdens and an obligation to hold a portion of deposits in reserves.
Ludwig's remarks were in a question and answer format in the Spring 1997 issue of Massachusetts Banker.
